title: Compose Production Infrastructure
objective: Compose roles and plays for highly available systems, logging, storage, and workstation automation.

sourceAlignment.title: Ansible for DevOps, 2nd Edition
sourceAlignment.author: Jeff Geerling
sourceAlignment.note: Original synthesis of the chapter's HA, ELK, GlusterFS, cloud, Vagrant, and macOS examples.

paragraphs: A production architecture is easier to automate when each tier has its own inventory group, play, and role. A site playbook imports the tier playbooks so the entire system can converge in a deliberate order.

Highly available stacks add load balancers, redundant application nodes, databases, and shared services. Logging pipelines centralize events; distributed storage introduces peer and quorum concerns. Cloud and local provisioners should feed the same configuration layer.

Workstation automation follows the same model: use localhost connection, package modules such as Homebrew integrations, and version-controlled dotfiles. Keep platform differences behind role variables and conditional task files.
explanation.rule: Compose small tier roles into a site playbook; do not build one monolithic list of tasks.

examples.title: Site Composition
examples.code:
- name: Configure load balancers
  hosts: load_balancers
  roles:
    - load_balancer
- name: Configure application nodes
  hosts: app_servers
  roles:
    - application
examples.note: Tier plays expose the architecture directly.

checks.question: What is the role of a site playbook?
options: Compose the plays that configure the whole system

feedback.incorrect: The site playbook is the orchestration entry point.
